Return CONFIRMED (reproduced from source), PLAUSIBLE (consistent with what you read, decisive evidence missing — say exactly what would settle it), or UNSUPPORTED (the citation doesn't support the claim — say what's actually true). The PR body and commit message both say `categories.performance` (found 0.29-0.41, needs ≥0.8) was "Not chased to 0.8 in this PR per the ticket's own instruction not to attempt a sweeping rewrite." Please re-pull SFCC-860 yourself (you have the same Atlassian MCP tools) and confirm independently: does any text anywhere on that ticket (description or comments) contain an instruction resembling "don't attempt a sweeping rewrite," or is that the PR author's own unminuted judgment call misattributed to the ticket?

`.github/workflows/deploy-sit.yml` (the file this PR edits) has `on: workflow_run: workflows: ['SIT Gate'], branches: ['release/**']` and job-level `if: ${{ github.event.workflow_run.conclusion == 'success' }}`. Then run `gh run list --repo ZimmermannAU/zimmermann-pwa --workflow "SIT Gate" --limit 5 --json databaseId,status,conclusion,headBranch,createdAt` — confirm the two most recent runs are both `conclusion: failure`. Then check `.github/workflows/digital-sit.yml` (the workflow literally named "SIT Gate") — confirm its `lighthouse-ci` job is a hard dependency of the gate's overall pass/fail (look for a `needs: [...]` job that gates on `lighthouse-ci`'s result). My claim: since this PR doesn't move `categories.performance` off ~0.3-0.4 (still under the required 0.8), the SIT Gate will keep failing overall even after this PR merges, which means `deploy-sit.yml` (this PR's own target file) will not auto-fire even on a fresh release branch cut after merge — and PR #78 targets `develop`, not `release/v0.1.0` (the one currently-open, currently-blocked release branch), so this fix doesn't even reach that branch without a separate forward-port. Confirm or refute each link in that chain from source, and say plainly whether the overall conclusion holds.

## F3 — CodeRabbit's Tier-1 approval was granted on the unverifiable reply, not the documented one
Run `gh api repos/ZimmermannAU/zimmermann-pwa/pulls/78/comments --jq '.[] | {id, user: .user.login, path, line, body: .body[0:300], created_at}'` and `gh pr view 78 --repo ZimmermannAU/zimmermann-pwa --json reviews` yourself. `.claude/rules/protectedFiles.md` lists `overrides/app/components/_app-config/` under "Global Shell" (Tier 2, "Owner: Both Squads — coordinate before touching"). `.claude/rules/frozenFiles.md` lists `.github/workflows/` under "CI/CD Pipeline" (Tier 1). AGENTS.md Hard Rule #10: "Never touch more than one protection tier in a single change without stopping to confirm scope with the developer." PR #78 touches both `.github/workflows/deploy-sit.yml` (Tier 1) and `overrides/app/components/_app-config/index.tsx` (Tier 2) in the same commit. Read the full PR body (`gh pr view 78 --repo ZimmermannAU/zimmermann-pwa --json body`) yourself and confirm: does it anywhere acknowledge touching two tiers at once and why that's acceptable scope for one PR, or does its "Tier 1 file touched" section only ever discuss `deploy-sit.yml` in isolation?

## F5 — The preconnect origin is very likely wrong for the actual page under test

Read `overrides/app/pages/home/index.tsx` at the PR's head commit yourself in full. My own read: `HomeNormal` fetches a Contentful `'homepage'` entry via `useContentfulEntries` purely as an existence gate (`if (!homepageContent) return null`) and then renders `<HomepageContent />`, whose only real output is `<ProductScroller products={productSearchResult?.hits} .../>` — SFCC product-search results, explicitly commented `// From PWA template - Example on how to show products`. `overrides/app/components/_app-config/index.tsx` (read the version currently on `develop`/at the PR's base commit — this code is NOT changed by this PR either way) mounts `<ContentfulLivePreviewProvider locale={locale} enableInspectorMode enableLiveUpdates>` unconditionally, for every route, with both flags forced `true`, no environment gate. Separately, check whether the codebase already has a narrower, correctly-scoped usage of the same provider elsewhere — look at `overrides/app/pages/contentfulPreview/index.tsx` and `overrides/app/pages/experience/index.tsx`. name: SIT Gate

on:
  push:
    branches:
      - 'release/**'
  pull_request:
    branches:
      - 'release/**'

permissions:
  contents: read
  issues: write
  pages: write
  id-token: write

jobs:
  playwright-p0:
    name: Playwright P0 journeys
    runs-on: ubuntu-latest
    continue-on-error: false
    steps:
      - uses: actions/checkout@v4

      - uses: actions/setup-node@v4
        with:
          node-version: '24'
          cache: 'npm'

      - name: Install dependencies
        run: npm install --include=dev

      - name: Install Playwright browsers
        run: node_modules/.bin/playwright install --with-deps chromium

      # Provisional: no *.p0.spec files exist anywhere in the repo yet (still early
      # development — see .docs/memory/projectState.md). --pass-with-no-tests keeps the
      # gate from permanently blocking every release branch on that basis alone, while a
      # real P0 spec that actually fails still fails the job normally — this only changes
      # the zero-tests case. The warning below keeps a "pass" from reading as real coverage —
      # scoped to match the `p0` Playwright project's own testDir/testMatch exactly
      # (playwright.config's testDir: './e2e', p0 project's testMatch: '**/*.p0.spec.{js,ts}'),
      # not just e2e/tests/zimm — a spec anywhere else under e2e/ that the project would
      # actually pick up must not trip a false "no coverage" warning.
      - name: Warn if no P0 specs exist yet
        run: |
          if ! find e2e -name '*.p0.spec.js' -o -name '*.p0.spec.ts' | grep -q .; then
            echo "::warning title=No P0 coverage::playwright-p0 passed with zero matching specs — this SIT gate is not verifying any P0 journey yet. See .claude/skills/qa-generate."
          fi

      - name: Run P0 suite
        run: node_modules/.bin/playwright test --project=p0 --reporter=html,github --pass-with-no-tests
        env:
          RETAIL_APP_HOME: ${{ vars.RETAIL_APP_HOME }}

      - name: Upload Playwright report
        if: always()
        uses: actions/upload-artifact@v4
        with:
          name: playwright-report
          path: playwright-report/
          retention-days: 30

      - name: Upload Pages artifact
        if: always()
        uses: actions/upload-pages-artifact@v3
        with:
          path: playwright-report/

  deploy-playwright-report:
    name: Publish Playwright report to Pages
    needs: playwright-p0
    if: always()
    runs-on: ubuntu-latest
    environment:
      name: github-pages
      url: ${{ steps.deployment.outputs.page_url }}
    steps:
      - name: Deploy to GitHub Pages
        id: deployment
        uses: actions/deploy-pages@v4

  lighthouse-ci:
    name: Lighthouse CI
    runs-on: ubuntu-latest
    continue-on-error: false
    env:
      LHCI_SERVER_BASE_URL: ${{ secrets.LHCI_SERVER_BASE_URL }}
      LHCI_TOKEN: ${{ secrets.LHCI_TOKEN }}
      LHCI_TARGET_URL: ${{ secrets.LHCI_TARGET_URL_SIT }}
    steps:
      - uses: actions/checkout@v4

      - uses: actions/setup-node@v4
        with:
          node-version: '24'
          cache: 'npm'

      - name: Install dependencies
        run: npm install --include=dev

      # SIT's MRT URL is access-controlled behind x-sfdc-access-control; see lighthouserc.js.
      # Step-scoped (not job-level) so npm install's lifecycle scripts — which inherit
      # job-level env but not this step's — never see the credential.
      - name: Run Lighthouse CI
        run: node_modules/.bin/lhci autorun
        env:
          LHCI_SFDC_ACCESS_CONTROL: ${{ secrets.LHCI_SFDC_ACCESS_CONTROL }}

      # Lighthouse records collect.settings.extraHeaders verbatim in each report's
      # configSettings — confirmed against a real run — so the access-control secret would
      # otherwise sit in plain text inside the artifact this job uploads next. Redact before
      # upload rather than trust nothing downstream ever inspects that field. Fail closed on a
      # jq error: the next step still runs on `if: always()`, so a report left unredacted by a
      # failed jq pass must not survive to be uploaded — delete it instead of uploading it as-is.
      - name: Redact secrets from Lighthouse reports before upload
        if: always()
        run: |
          shopt -s nullglob
          for f in .lighthouseci/lhr-*.json; do
            if ! jq '.configSettings.extraHeaders |= (if . then with_entries(.value = "[REDACTED]") else . end)' "$f" > "$f.tmp"; then
              rm -f "$f" "$f.tmp"
              continue
            fi
            mv "$f.tmp" "$f"
          done

      - name: Upload Lighthouse results
        if: always()
        uses: actions/upload-artifact@v4
        with:
          name: lighthouse-results
          path: .lighthouseci/
          retention-days: 30

  contract-tests:
    name: MuleSoft contract tests
    runs-on: ubuntu-latest
    continue-on-error: false
    steps:
      - uses: actions/checkout@v4

      - uses: actions/setup-node@v4
        with:
          node-version: '24'
          cache: 'npm'

      - name: Install dependencies
        run: npm install --include=dev

      # TODO: Replace with real contract assertion once MuleSoft publishes OpenAPI specs.
      # Owner: Zimmermann integration team + Accenture delivery lead to align.
      - name: Run contract tests
        run: npm run test:contracts

  bundle-size:
    name: Bundle size check
    runs-on: ubuntu-latest
    continue-on-error: false
    steps:
      - uses: actions/checkout@v4

      - uses: actions/setup-node@v4
        with:
          node-version: '24'
          cache: 'npm'

      - name: Install dependencies
        run: npm install --include=dev

      - name: Build and check bundle size
        run: npm run test:max-file-size

  sit-gate:
    name: SIT Gate
    needs: [playwright-p0, lighthouse-ci, contract-tests, bundle-size]
    runs-on: ubuntu-latest
    if: always()
    steps:
      - name: Check all SIT signals passed
        run: |
          if [ "${{ needs.playwright-p0.result }}" != "success" ] || \
             [ "${{ needs.lighthouse-ci.result }}" != "success" ] || \
             [ "${{ needs.contract-tests.result }}" != "success" ] || \
             [ "${{ needs.bundle-size.result }}" != "success" ]; then
            echo "SIT gate: one or more checks failed"
            echo "  playwright-p0:   ${{ needs.playwright-p0.result }}"
            echo "  lighthouse-ci:   ${{ needs.lighthouse-ci.result }}"
            echo "  contract-tests:  ${{ needs.contract-tests.result }}"
            echo "  bundle-size:     ${{ needs.bundle-size.result }}"
            exit 1
          fi
          echo "SIT gate: all checks passed"
